subject: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@finservco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up

Hi Morgan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

Call recap
- Primary goal: replace legacy inference stack for real-time fraud scoring + post-chat summarization.
- Key constraints: PII in requests, strict data residency (US only), target 99.95% availability, sub-200ms p95 latency for scoring requests.
- Expected steady-state: ~300 QPS scoring calls (avg 120 tokens/request) and ~50 QPS async summarization bursts. Monthly token estimate: ~2.6B tokens.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 and audit evidence required; legal will ask about data retention & access controls.

Deployment modes discussed
- Hosted API: fastest start, per-token economics, shared tenancy, Redwood-managed security posture.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool, predictability for throughput and cost, can be scoped to region and isolated tenancy.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed network, full control for regulatory needs — longer lead time, higher fixed costs.

From today’s signals you gave, it sounds like Dedicated or Private are the most likely fits given data residency and SLA needs, but Hosted could be used for a pilot if we can meet your data controls.

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll loop in our pricing/product SME to model three scenarios (hosted per-token pilot, dedicated reserved commit 3/12/36 month, private deployment estimate).
2) We’ll include a cost table showing per-token vs reserved capacity break-even and expected monthly run-rate.
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min pricing walkthrough with your infra/security team next week.

Action items for you
- Confirm whether you need on-prem (air-gapped) vs VPC (customer-managed cloud) for Private.
- Share any internal SLA/uptime targets beyond 99.95% or any procurement timeline constraints.

I’ll send the pricing models by EOD tomorrow. Thanks —
— Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123
redwoodinference.com

From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@finservco.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 17:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up

Thanks Aditya — great summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: must be US-only. VPC deployment in our AWS account would be preferred over on-prem right now.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence is necessary; we’ll want to review controls around key management and access logs.
- SLA: 99.95% is the right bar. We may ask for 99.99% for a small set of critical endpoints later but not required for pilot.
- Timeline: procurement window is aggressive — ideally want commercial terms in 4–6 weeks, pilot starting in 8–10 weeks.

Also: can you give a sense of the break-even point where Dedicated reserved capacity becomes cheaper than Hosted per-token for our 2.6B tokens/month case?

I’m copying our infra/ops lead offline if needed.

— Morgan
Director, ML Platforms | FinServ Co
morgan.lee@finservco.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@finservco.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up — pricing model request

Marissa / Neha — forwarding Morgan’s clarifications. Can you help model three scenarios for RINF-2026-0534: hosted pilot, 12-month dedicated reserved commit, and private VPC (customer AWS account) estimate. Key inputs below (from call):

Inputs
- Monthly tokens: 2.6B tokens (mix: 85% scoring / 15% summarization)
- Peak scoring: 300 QPS (low token per request ~120) with occasional 50 QPS burst for summaries
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for scoring path
- Data residency: US-only; Private should be VPC in customer AWS account if possible
- Timeline: final commercial terms in 4–6 weeks, pilot start 8–10 weeks

Please include in the model:
- Unit economics: per-token hosted price assumptions, equivalent cost if served on dedicated pool (GPU-hour + infra + network), and amortized private deployment setup costs + O&M.
- Break-even analysis: given the inputs, what monthly token volume makes dedicated cheaper than hosted? Provide 3 commit lengths (3/12/36).
- Assumptions: list quantization/throughput model (e.g., gpt-small-quantized per-GPU throughput), average tokens per second during peaks, and any required support/managed services line items.

Attach a one-page pricing matrix and a SOC2 evidence stub. I’ll review and send to Morgan.

Thanks —
Aditya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@finservco.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up — pricing matrix attached

Hi team — attached is a preliminary pricing matrix and SOC2 evidence summary (see attachments). High-level takeaways below: 

Summary (preliminary)
- Hosted (pilot): assumed list price $0.0006 per token for generation-equivalent workload, with pilot discounts available. Estimated monthly cost @2.6B tokens: ~$1.56M/mo. Pros: fastest to start, minimal infra ops. Cons: shared tenancy and higher variable spend.
- Dedicated (reserved): modeled on a 12-month reserved commit covering expected peak concurrency. Estimated committed monthly cost: ~$420k/mo (amortized GPU + infra + support). Break-even vs hosted occurs around ~630M tokens/mo for 12-month commit; at 2.6B tokens/mo dedicated is ~3.7x cheaper on unit economics. 3/36 month commit delta and sensitivity included in sheet.
- Private (VPC customer AWS): one-time onboarding/setup ~$120k (secure networking, KMS integration, audit logging), ongoing monthly infra + support estimated ~$480k/mo (higher ops overhead but full tenancy & control). For strictly regulatory-driven customers who need VPC, this is the model we recommend.

Assumptions & notes
- Throughput assumptions based on quantized model profile: 1x V100-equivalent GPU = 125 tokens/sec for scoring workload; effective concurrency provisioning set to ensure p95 <200ms.
- Included support: 24x7 paging for dedicated + private; hosted includes standard business hours support with SLA upgrade add-on.
- All numbers exclude tax and third-party cloud egress/net charges (estimated separately).

Attachments
- RINF_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (breakdown by scenario, commit length sensitivity, assumptions)
- SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf (control mappings, evidence list; full packet available on request)

Next steps
1) Aditya: share this with Morgan and propose a 30-min walkthrough later this week.
2) If Morgan confirms VPC path, we’ll produce a short SOW + 12-month commercial term suggestion for procurement.

Happy to walk through the sheet — I included model tabs for 3/12/36 month commits and a break-even chart.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Pricing & GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up — pricing matrix

Morgan — attaching the pricing matrix and SOC2 summary from Marissa (see attached files). TL;DR: for your 2.6B tokens/mo profile Dedicated reserved commit (12-month) is materially cheaper (~$420k/mo) versus Hosted (~$1.56M/mo). Private (VPC) has a moderate one-time onboarding cost but gives you the tenancy and controls you asked for (~$480k/mo ongoing estimate).

Proposed next steps
- Quick 30-min walkthrough: I’m available Thu 11:00–12:00 PT or Fri 09:00–10:00 PT. Which works?
- If you want to proceed down VPC: we’ll prepare a 12-month SOW + onboarding timeline (estimate 6–8 weeks to get VPC in your AWS account configured and security review completed).

Would love to lock a time for the walkthrough and confirm procurement timeline.
\Thanks —
